I will keep chrysanthemum on the full 35.0 mu this year. I have done this crop for many years, so I do not start from zero; I start from what usually gives me stable flowers and then adjust for cost and field condition. On chrysanthemum, I do not like to cut fertilizer too hard, because once the plants stay short or the buds are weak, I cannot recover the season easily. Since I have well irrigation, I can push growth more steadily than relying on rain, so I will use improved planting material, plough the land first, and then manage water and fertilizer in a more even way through the season. For nutrition, I will keep nitrogen a bit higher to support stem and leaf growth early, but I will also hold phosphorus and potassium at a solid level because flower crops need good rooting, stem strength, and flower quality. My farm is 35 mu, so I also think about labor efficiency. I will keep the plan simple enough that one person can manage it with hired help only at busy times. I will not gamble on very low input use. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and crop protection than lose flower yield and quality.
